cleanIntro: Read what this book is before you use it. The Renegauge shipped with a twelve-page instruction guide, and Savage points past it in its own opening — for more information and for expanded instruction guides, visit savagearms.com. What it does publish it publishes properly: safety operation, loading, firing, unloading, barrel removal, the magazine plug, and choke tubes. What it does not publish is any cleaning or lubrication procedure whatsoever. There is no bore-cleaning routine, no solvent guidance, no lubrication points, no bolt or carrier removal, no gas-system disassembly and no trigger-group removal anywhere in the document — the word cleaning appears in it only in the warranty exclusions. So the guide below stops where the book stops: unload it, take the barrel off, and go no further than the magazine plug and the choke tubes. Nothing deeper has been invented to fill the gap, and anything you have read elsewhere about stripping a Renegauge's gas system is not in the manual Savage put in the box.

steps.title: This is the short guide, and Savage says so
steps.action: Set your expectations from the book itself. This twelve-page guide covers safety, loading, firing, unloading, barrel removal, the magazine plug and choke tubes — and Savage's own opening page directs you to the website for more information and for expanded instruction guides. That is a real bound on what follows. In particular there is no cleaning section, no lubrication instruction and no procedure for taking the bolt, the carrier or the gas system out, so nothing below will tell you to do any of those things. Treat a procedure you find elsewhere as unsourced against this document.
steps.prose: That absence is worth stating plainly rather than papering over: the manufacturer published a field strip and stopped.
steps.caution: No cleaning, lubrication or gas-system procedure is published in this manual.
steps.quote: For more information, and for expanded instruction guides, please visit www.savagearms.com or contact Savage Arms at 1-800-370-0708.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Introduction, p.1

steps.title: The safety does not put itself back on
steps.action: Find the safety selector at the rear of the trigger guard and understand its one behaviour that catches people out: it does not move to full safe on its own when the bolt is opened and closed. It is manual in both directions. A pump or a bolt gun that resets its own safety teaches a habit this shotgun will not honour, so every time the action is cycled the selector is wherever you last put it. Push it across to full safe by hand and confirm it before anything else happens.
steps.quote: The Renegauge family of shotguns employs a manual, two-position safety – Full Safe and Ready to Fire. The safety selector does not automatically move to the full safe position when the bolt is opened and closed. It must be moved manually.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Safety Operation, p.2
steps.warn: The safety never re-engages itself. Set it by hand, every time.

steps.title: Red band showing means ready to fire
steps.action: Read the selector rather than feeling for it. When the red band is visible the safety is off and the shotgun is ready to fire; when the band is hidden the safety is on. Push the selector to either side to change it. The band is the whole indication — there is no click sequence to count and no lettering to read in poor light — so make the check visual and make it every time you pick the gun up, including now, before the barrel comes off.
steps.quote: When the Red Band is visible, the safety is off – Ready to Fire position – see Figure 1. When the Red Band is hidden from view, the safety is on – Full Safe position – see Figure 2.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Safety Operation, p.2

steps.title: Charging handle back — that clears the chamber only
steps.action: With the safety at full safe and the muzzle in a safe direction, pull the charging handle rearward to extract and eject whatever is in the chamber, then let it return forward carefully. This clears one shell and one shell only. The magazine tube is still loaded at this point, and on this shotgun a loaded tube does not empty itself by cycling the action — there is a separate sequence below for that. Do not treat an ejected shell as evidence the gun is empty.
steps.quote: Pull rearward on the Charging Handle – see Figure 15. This will extract and eject a live cartridge from the chamber.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Unloading Procedure, p.6

steps.title: Press the elevator down to reach the cartridge stop
steps.action: Now empty the magazine tube, which is a two-handed job on a Renegauge. Depress the cartridge elevator to get access to the cartridge stop, which sits at the side of the magazine tube behind it. The elevator is the shelf that lifts a shell to the chamber, and until it is pushed down out of the way your fingers cannot reach past it. Work through the loading port with the gun pointed somewhere safe and the safety on.
steps.quote: Depress the Cartridge Elevator – see Figure 16 - to gain access to the Cartridge Stop, at the side of the Magazine Tube.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Unloading Procedure, p.7

steps.title: Cartridge stop outward, and a shell releases
steps.action: At the base of the cartridge, press the cartridge stop towards the outside of the shotgun. That releases one shell from the magazine tube into your hand — take it out of the gun before doing anything else. The stop is what holds the whole column against the magazine spring, so expect the shell to come forward with some urgency rather than to fall out. One press, one shell; the stop resets behind it and holds the next.
steps.quote: At the base of the cartridge, press the Cartridge Stop towards the outside of the shotgun – see Figure 17. This will allow a cartridge to release from the magazine tube. Remove the cartridge from the shotgun.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Unloading Procedure, p.7

steps.title: Repeat until you can see the red follower
steps.action: Keep repeating the elevator-and-stop sequence until the red magazine follower is visible at the end of the magazine tube. The follower is the confirmation, not the shell count — a magazine plug, a different tube length or a shell that has been in there since last season all make counting unreliable, and red is visible from outside the gun in poor light. Do not stop pressing the cartridge stop until you have seen it.
steps.prose: That same red follower is what the assembly section has you look for before putting the barrel on.
steps.quote: Repeat steps 4 & 5 until the red Magazine Follower is visible at the end of the Magazine Tube – see Figure 18.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Unloading Procedure, p.7
steps.warn: The red follower showing is the only proof the tube is empty.

steps.title: Lock the bolt back and check the chamber with eye and hand
steps.action: Press rearward on the cartridge release lever and pull the charging handle back to lock the bolt and carrier assembly to the rear, then check the chamber both by looking and by feeling. Savage asks for both — visibly and physically — and on a 12 gauge with a deep receiver that is not belt and braces: a shell resting on the elevator can sit outside the light from the ejection port. Only after the chamber is confirmed empty and the follower is showing is the gun ready to come apart.
steps.quote: Visibly and physically inspect the chamber to be clear of ammunition.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Unloading Procedure, p.7
steps.warn: Chamber and magazine tube both, by eye and by hand.

steps.title: Ride the bolt closed — hold the handle while you release the carrier
steps.action: The barrel will not come off with the bolt locked back, so close it under control. Hold the charging handle rearward with one hand, depress the carrier release lever with the other, and let the bolt and carrier assembly move fully forward at a speed you are choosing. Then press forward on the charging handle to be certain the bolt is all the way home. The order is the whole instruction: the handle is held first, the release is pressed second.
steps.quote: While holding the Charging Handle rearward, depress the Carrier Release Lever – see item 1 in Figure 20. Carefully allow the Bolt/Carrier Assembly to move fully forward – see item 2 in Figure 20.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Barrel Removal, p.8

steps.title: Let go of the handle first and the carrier slams
steps.action: Savage spells out what happens if the sequence is reversed, and it is worth reading before rather than after: press the carrier release lever without the charging handle held back and the bolt and carrier assembly slam forward with extreme force. Keep fingers clear of the ejection port throughout. On a gas gun with a heavy carrier this is a genuine injury, not a pinch, and it is also how the front of the ejection port gets battered by the charging handle. Hold the handle, then release.
steps.quote: CAUTION – if the charging handle is not held rearward and the carrier release lever is depressed, the bolt/carrier assembly will slam forward with extreme force. Be sure to keep fingers clear of the ejection port.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Barrel Removal, p.8
steps.warn: Fingers clear of the ejection port. Hold the handle before releasing the carrier.

steps.title: Magazine cap off — it clicks as it comes
steps.action: Unscrew and remove the magazine cap from the front of the magazine tube. It clicks audibly as it turns, which is a detent doing its job rather than a fault, and the clicking is also how you know the cap is moving rather than the whole fore-end turning with it. Take the cap right off and put it somewhere it will not roll away — it is the only thing holding the barrel and fore-end assembly on the gun.
steps.quote: Unscrew and remove the Magazine Cap, an audible clicking noise will be heard – see Figure 21.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Barrel Removal, p.8

steps.title: Barrel and fore-end forward, off the tube
steps.action: Grasp the barrel forward of the magazine tube and pull it carefully away from the receiver. The barrel and fore-end come off as one assembly, sliding forward off the magazine tube and out of the receiver together. Two things want care: support the weight as the barrel extension leaves the receiver so it does not lever against the mouth, and do not let the charging handle forcefully impact the front of the ejection port as the assembly clears. Straight forward, level, and lift it away.
steps.caution: Do not let the charging handle strike the front of the ejection port.
steps.quote: Grasp the Barrel forward of the magazine tube and carefully pull away from the Receiver. Be careful not to let the Charging Handle forcefully impact the front of the Ejection Port. The Barrel and Fore-end Assembly will slide out of and away from the receiver and magazine tube – see Figure 22.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Barrel Removal, p.8

steps.title: Put the cap back on the bare tube
steps.action: With the barrel off, screw the magazine cap back onto the magazine tube until it is snug and the clicking stops. Savage prints this as a numbered step of barrel removal rather than as tidiness, and there is a reason to obey it: the cap on the bare tube keeps the threads clean, keeps the detent from being knocked about, and means the one small part you cannot shoot the gun without is attached to the gun rather than loose on the bench. Take it off again only when you are working on the magazine plug.
steps.quote: Reinstall the Magazine Cap onto the magazine tube until snug and the clicking noise stops – see Figure 23.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Barrel Removal, p.8

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: In front of you should be the receiver with its bolt and carrier still inside, and the barrel and fore-end assembly as one piece. That is the entire published owner disassembly for a Renegauge — the bolt, the carrier, the gas system and the trigger group all stay in the gun, because no procedure for removing any of them appears in this manual. Inspect what you can now reach: look through the barrel for ammunition, obstructions and debris, and check the magazine tube by looking for the red follower at the rear of it. Deep Clean covers the choke tubes and the magazine plug, which are the only two things Savage publishes beyond this point.
steps.quote: Ensure that the barrel is clear of any ammunition or debris by looking through the barrel before assembly. Ensure that the magazine tube contains no ammunition by visually noting the red magazine follower at the rear of the tube.
steps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Assembly Procedure, p.3

deepSteps.title: Choke tube out, counterclockwise, with the wrench engaged
deepSteps.action: Confirm the shotgun is unloaded and the safety selector is at full safe, then insert the choke tube wrench so it properly engages the notches in the tube and turn counterclockwise to remove. Engaging the notches fully before applying force is the whole job — a wrench that is only half in rounds the notches, and a rounded choke tube in a barrel is a job for someone with the right extractor and a lot of patience. Take the tube right out and look at the threads in the barrel while they are exposed.
deepSteps.quote: Insert the Choke Tube Wrench and engage the notches in the Choke Tube. Turn counterclockwise to remove – see Figure 30.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Choke Tube Installation/Removal, p.11

deepSteps.title: Clean the threads before a new tube goes in
deepSteps.action: With the tube out, clean the threads before installing anything. Plastic wad residue and powder fouling build up in the thread root and in the relief cut ahead of it, and a tube driven onto dirty threads seats crooked, comes loose under recoil, or seizes. Savage puts the instruction between removal and installation for that reason. Clean both halves — the tube's own threads and the barrel's — then insert the new tube by hand until it stops before any wrench touches it.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the Choke Tube. Be sure to clean the threads before a new tube is installed. Insert a new Choke Tube into the barrel.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Choke Tube Installation/Removal, p.11

deepSteps.title: Strong hand tight — about 65 inch-pounds — and oil is optional
deepSteps.action: Tighten a removable choke tube to a strong hand tight, which Savage puts at approximately 65 inch-pounds. Threads must be clear of debris going in, and a light coating of gun oil may be applied to them if you want it. That last part is the only lubrication instruction of any kind in this manual, and it is about the choke threads specifically, not about the shotgun. Do not read it as licence to oil anything else here — there is no lubrication section in this book to read.
deepSteps.prose: Sixty-five inch-pounds is firm thumb-and-finger pressure on a choke wrench, not a lever.
deepSteps.caution: About 65 inch-pounds. No published lubrication anywhere else in this manual.
deepSteps.quote: It is recommended to tighten removeable choke tubes to a strong hand tight – approximately 65 inch-pounds. Be sure that the threads are clear of debris when installing. A light coating of gun oil may be applied to the threads if desired.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Choke Tubes, p.10

deepSteps.title: Check how the tube sits before the barrel goes back
deepSteps.action: Look at the installed tube from the muzzle before reassembling. A flush mount choke tube should sit flush with the end of the barrel and not protrude at all; an extended tube's shoulder should sit tight against the barrel. Either way the tell is the same — a gap, or a flush tube standing proud, means it is not fully home or the threads are dirty, and firing it like that damages the barrel and the choke threads. Back it out, clean, and start again rather than tightening harder.
deepSteps.quote: Flush mount choke tubes should sit flush with the end of the barrel and not protrude. The shoulder on extended choke tubes should sit tight to the barrel.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Choke Tube Installation/Removal, p.11
deepSteps.warn: A tube that is not fully seated must not be fired.

deepSteps.title: Read the tube before you decide what to shoot through it
deepSteps.action: Every removable Renegauge choke tube is marked with its constriction and with the shot materials it is rated to handle, and Savage's instruction is to shoot only what your particular tube is rated for. Steel and tungsten through a tube rated for lead is the case that bites: the named consequence is damage to the choke tube, the shotgun, the shooter and bystanders. Read the marking on the tube in your hand rather than remembering what you fitted last season, and check it again after any tube swap.
deepSteps.quote: Be sure to check that the shot material selection is compatible with the choke tubes installed in the shotgun (if applicable). Using a material that is too hard may cause damage to the choke tube, shotgun, the shooter or other bystanders.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Ammunition, p.2
deepSteps.warn: Never fire a shot material the fitted choke tube is not rated for.

deepSteps.title: Magazine plug: barrel off, tube empty, thumb on the end cap
deepSteps.action: The magazine plug lives behind the magazine tube end cap and the barrel has to be off to reach it. Confirm the shotgun is clear and the safety is at full safe, take the magazine cap off, then press the magazine tube end cap into the tube with your thumb and keep it there. That thumb is doing real work from this point on — it is the only thing containing the magazine spring — so set yourself up with the gun braced and the far end of the tube pointed away from your face before you go on.
deepSteps.quote: With the barrel and the magazine cap removed, depress the Magazine Tube End Cap into the Magazine Tube with your thumb – see Figure 24.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Magazine Plug Installation/Removal, p.9

deepSteps.title: Drive the retention pin out while the cap stays pressed in
deepSteps.action: With the end cap held down, use a small punch or screwdriver to press the magazine tube end cap retention pin out through the tube — it can go either direction, so use whichever side gives you a straight approach. Keep depressing the end cap the whole time and continue holding it as the pin comes fully out. The moment the pin clears, the only thing left restraining the spring is your thumb, which is precisely the position the next warning is about.
deepSteps.quote: With a small punch or screwdriver, press the Magazine Tube End Cap Retention Pin through the magazine tube from either direction – see Figure 25.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Magazine Plug Installation/Removal, p.9

deepSteps.title: That end cap is under extreme spring tension
deepSteps.action: Savage prints this caution twice on the same page, which is unusual enough to take literally: the magazine tube end cap is under extreme spring tension, it will be launched into the air if pressure is lost, and your face must be kept away from the magazine tube. Maintain pressure throughout. A full-length 12 gauge magazine spring stores a lot of energy and the end cap is a small hard part travelling in a straight line out of a tube. Safety glasses, face out of line, and both hands committed.
deepSteps.quote: CAUTION – The Magazine Tube End Cap is under extreme spring tension. Be sure to maintain pressure on the Magazine Tube End Cap, otherwise it may be launched into the air. Be sure to keep your face away from the Magazine Tube at this point.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Magazine Plug Installation/Removal, p.9
deepSteps.warn: Keep your face out of line with the magazine tube. Never release the end cap suddenly.

deepSteps.title: Let the cap come out under control, and the spring is exposed
deepSteps.action: Wrap your hands around and over the top of the magazine tube end cap and let it come out of the tube slowly, still contained. Once it is out, the magazine spring is exposed and free. Now the plug can be inserted into or removed from the centre of the spring — that is the entire purpose of everything above. Keep the spring in a straight line rather than letting it kink; a bent magazine spring is a shotgun that stops feeding the last shell out of the tube.
deepSteps.quote: Wrap your hands around and over the top of the Magazine Tube End Cap and carefully allow it to come out of the Magazine Tube. See Figure 26. The Magazine Spring will be exposed once the Magazine Tube End Cap is removed.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Magazine Plug Installation/Removal, p.9

deepSteps.title: Going back: notches outward, pin flush both sides
deepSteps.action: Compress the spring back into the tube until it is flush with the end, then fit the end cap over it with the notched end facing away from the magazine tube — that orientation is what lets the pin pass. Line up the holes in the end cap and the tube and push the retention pin through. The check is unambiguous and worth doing every time: a correctly seated pin sits flush with both sides of the magazine tube. A pin standing proud on one side is not through both walls of the tube and will not hold the spring.
deepSteps.caution: Flush on BOTH sides, or the pin is not through.
deepSteps.quote: Line up the holes in the Magazine Tube End Cap and the Magazine Tube and insert the Magazine Tube End Cap Retention Pin through the holes – see Figure 28. Once the Magazine Tube End Cap Retention Pin is seated properly, it will be flush with both sides of the Magazine Tube – see Figure 29.
deepSteps.cite: RENEGAUGE — Rev. 0 (12/19) — printed as "114644 (12/19) Rev. 0" — Magazine Plug Installation/Removal, p.10

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHOKE
tasks: Look through the barrel and confirm it is clear of ammunition, obstructions and debris
Choke tube out with the wrench fully engaged in the notches, counterclockwise
Clean both sets of threads — the tube's and the barrel's — before anything is refitted
Refit to a strong hand tight, about 65 inch-pounds; a light coat of gun oil on the threads is optional
Flush tubes sit flush; extended tubes sit shoulder-tight. Never fire a tube that is not fully seated
Check the tube's marked shot-material rating against what you intend to shoot

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Confirm the tube is empty — the red magazine follower must be visible at the end of the tube
Keep the magazine cap on the bare tube while the barrel is off, snug until the clicking stops
If the plug is being changed: barrel off, cap off, thumb on the end cap before the pin moves
The end cap is under extreme spring tension — face out of line, pressure maintained throughout
On reassembly the retention pin must sit flush with BOTH sides of the tube

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & ACTION — WHAT IS PUBLISHED
tasks: The bolt, carrier, gas system and trigger group stay in the gun — no removal procedure is published
Keep fingers clear of the ejection port whenever the carrier release is touched
Hold the charging handle rearward before depressing the carrier release, always
Do not let the charging handle strike the front of the ejection port during barrel removal
⛔ This manual publishes NO cleaning solvent, lubrication or interval guidance. Savage directs owners to its expanded instruction guides

reassembly: Confirm the barrel is clear of ammunition and debris by looking through it, and confirm the magazine tube is empty by noting the red magazine follower at the rear of the tube.
Place the safety selector into the Full Safe position.
Unscrew and remove the magazine cap; the carrier assembly will move forward slightly and the charging handle will rest at the front of the ejection port.
Ensure the fore-end is seated fully forward on the barrel assembly.
Slide the barrel assembly onto the magazine tube, aligning the barrel extension into the receiver and around the bolt assembly.
Ensure the barrel assembly is fully seated into the receiver before the cap goes near it.
Reinstall the magazine cap onto the magazine tube until snug and the clicking noise stops.
Press rearward on the cartridge release lever, then pull rearward on the charging handle to lock the bolt open.
Ensure the barrel is clear of obstructions before the shotgun is fired.
fncheck: With the shotgun reassembled and unloaded, confirm the barrel assembly is fully seated in the receiver and the magazine cap is snug with the clicking stopped — a cap that still clicks is not tight. Press rearward on the cartridge release lever and pull the charging handle back; the bolt and carrier assembly should lock to the rear. Check the chamber visibly and physically once more, and confirm the red magazine follower is visible at the end of the magazine tube. Hold the charging handle rearward, depress the carrier release lever and ride the bolt fully forward, then press forward on the charging handle to confirm the bolt is fully closed. Work the safety selector both ways and confirm the red band appears and disappears cleanly, remembering that it will not re-engage itself when the action is cycled. Finally confirm any fitted choke tube is seated — flush tubes flush, extended tubes shoulder-tight — and that the barrel is clear of obstructions before shooting.
